propositions: Accepted /rerun and recheck-review requests exist only as transient _rebar_force events in the process-local asyncio queue and disappear on process loss or shutdown before dequeue
After process loss, Gerrit retains the nonzero LLM-Review vote and SQLite retains the matching voted row, causing reconciliation to skip the revision and fail to re-review

The durability repair requires accepted requests to reset the exact revision to neutral LLM-Review: 0 before acknowledgement, emitting a patchset-bearing comment-added event that re-admits old changes to the reconciler's bounded events-log window

Reconciliation must query Gerrit before consulting local dedup; a definitive no-nonzero-vote read clears only the exact stale dedup row and proceeds to review, while Gerrit errors preserve dedup and hold the cursor for retry

Contributor text cannot select label values or mint PASS/BLOCK; only the privileged reset operation writes the fixed neutral value 0, and affirmative/refusal replies remain label-free via post_comment

Process restart recovery is proven by a stateful integration test in which /rerun returns 202 with queued state, the old process queue is discarded, a replacement queue starts empty, and one reconcile pass consumes the reset-emitted event and casts exactly one new vote for the same revision
